title: The read-only layer, the refusal test, one validation level everywhere (harness learning, H1)
request: The owner asked to continue the harness-learning plan through H2. H1 comes before anything learns: the harness reports named editable guardrails as a risk that needs code, not prompts (Harness2 let its editor delete safety rules), and one validation level everywhere (item 4 of the first report).
spec: Plan 'improve the harness so it learns', package H1: a list of protected paths and a diff check refusing any learned change to them; a fixed list of bad moves the validator, the loop, the registry, the gateway and the grader must still refuse after every candidate (100% or the candidate is dropped); full schema checks for the Toolbox (the intern's standard plan, MCP clients) and the Home agent's code-made calls.
plan: read the validator's holdout rule, the registry's checks and guards, the three tool entry points and the gateway's reserve
protected.py: the layer and check_diff / check_git
refusal.py: eleven cases each driving the real guard with no model and no spend; the refusal command and make target
Toolbox.call and HomeAgent.run_tool to schema checks; the tests that pinned the old leniency updated
tests: the layer, every case refused today, a weakened guard reported, every entry point checking types

decisions.decision: The refusal test drives the real guards, not copies of their rules
decisions.why: a copy would keep passing after the guard itself was weakened

decisions.decision: A test loosens three guards on purpose and the refusal test must report each
decisions.why: a test that cannot fail proves nothing

decisions.decision: Each case checks the specific rule fired, not any refusal
decisions.why: the toy project is refused for having no solution too; the holdout case requires the holdout rule itself to fail, the order case the edge rule

decisions.decision: The whole learning harness and its campaign are protected
decisions.why: the grader's door, the gate and this layer must not be editable by what they judge; a skill (H4) lives in its own folder outside them

decisions.decision: The Toolbox and the Home agent's code calls move to full schema checks
decisions.why: the intern's model calls already run on run() with them; a wrong type or a value out of bounds now comes back as an error to read, never a crash inside a handler

change: dclab_rnd/learning/protected.py and refusal.py (new); dclab_rnd/learning/__main__.py (refusal); dclab_rnd/intern/tools.py (check=schema); dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py (check=schema); Makefile (refusal-test); tests/test_learning_h1.py (new); tests/test_agents_runtime.py and test_draft_flow.py (the leniency they pinned replaced by the new rule); tests/test_agent_harness.py (the refusal test listed as a measurement harness).

findings.defect: a wrong argument type sent through the Toolbox reached its handler and crashed it
findings.scenario: describe_data with project_id 5: TypeError inside the handler
findings.cause: the Toolbox checked argument names only, a level kept until the intern moved onto run(), which it had
findings.fix: schema checks at every entry point
findings.impact: a crash where an error to read was due

findings.defect: two tests pinned the old leniency: a string number coerced, an offset of 'x' ignored, values outside the schema's bounds clamped
findings.cause: the leniency was the documented behaviour until this package
findings.fix: the tests assert the new rule: a readable error naming the argument and its bound; valid calls unchanged
findings.impact: a deliberate change of behaviour, approved with the reports' item 4

findings.defect: the guards that call the validator were outside the layer, and the refusal test never went through them
findings.scenario: a learned change setting the Toolbox guard's actor to 'human' passed check_diff, and the refusal test still showed 11 of 11 while the agent could reuse the holdout
findings.cause: a deny list of files that named the validator but not its callers
findings.fix: the layer is an allow list (a learned change writes only skills/), the deny list a second check naming every guard; the two validator cases run through the Toolbox's guard on a real project; a test loosens the guard exactly as the attack did and the refusal test reports it
findings.impact: the holdout reusable by a learned change

findings.defect: a renamed protected file was listed by its new name only
findings.scenario: git mv of the grader into skills/ returned nothing
findings.fix: --no-renames --raw: a rename is a deletion and an addition; a symbolic link refused by its mode
findings.impact: the grader movable out of the layer

findings.defect: an upper-case path got past the list; the Mac's disk opens it as the real file
findings.cause: a case-sensitive comparison on a case-insensitive disk
findings.impact: the validator writable by its upper-case name

findings.defect: the list missed the tests, the Makefile, the repository's hooks and settings, the gates H5 must pass, the purposes and routing
findings.scenario: a learned refusal-test target set to true would pass
findings.cause: a deny list always misses something
findings.fix: the allow list; the deny list extended for readers
findings.impact: a gate disabled by what it judges

findings.defect: the refusal command printed its verdict and kept nothing
findings.impact: a gate run unrecorded (the owner's rule)

measurements.name: the refusal test on today's code
measurements.result: 11 of 11 refused, the two validator cases through the Toolbox's own guard; four guards loosened in a test, each reported
measurements.next: run after every learned candidate (H3 onwards)
limits: eleven cases: a guard the list does not name is not tested

measurements.name: the 47 test files driving the Toolbox, MCP or Home tools
measurements.gate: every test passes with schema checks
measurements.result: 861 tests; three failed (the two pinned leniencies and the harness rule), all fixed

outcome: Nothing learned can change the validator, the caps, the loop, the grader, the generator, the prompts or the learning harness; eleven bad moves are refused by the real guards with no model and no spend; every tool entry point checks argument types as the loop does.
lessons: Prove a guard test can fail by loosening the guard in a test.
When a leniency was a placeholder for a later move, remove it when the move lands.
risks: H5's candidate prompts need their own entry in the allow list when H5 is built
MCP clients that send a number as text now get an error instead of a conversion: no MCP-level test covers it
